newsitem.title: INDIA: Adviser to India PM quits after one day on the job.
newsitem.headline: Adviser to India PM quits after one day on the job.

text.p: A foreign affairs adviser to Indian Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral resigned on Tuesday after one day in office following lawmakers' calls that he be sacked for his controversial views, the Press Trust of India said.
The news agency said Bhabani Sengupta, who assumed office on Monday after Gujral hand-picked him last week as a special adviser, resigned after an uproar in parliament.
Sengupta, a foreign affairs analyst at a private New Delhi-based think tank, was known to hold unusual views on sensitive national security issues.
He had urged India to renounce its longstanding option to build nuclear weapons, a possibility it has kept open since conducting its only nuclear test in 1974.
Sengupta had also advocated ceding disputed territory to neighbouring Pakistan, with which India has fought three wars since 1947.
Gujral had been due to make a statement in parliament on Sengupta's appointment on Wednesday. Sengupta was not immediately available for comment.
